tables.heading_context: ## The 8 Fallacies of Distributed Computing (Peter Deutsch, 1994)
rows: Networks drop packets, TCP connections reset, VMs disappear
TFS agent drops mid-build; work item API times out
P2 build queries from West US to East US
You cannot stream unlimited data; TCP backpressure kicks in
Git clone of a large mono-repo saturates bandwidth
VSTS service-to-service calls inside Azure still need mTLS
IPs change, VMs migrate, AZs fail, DNS propagates slowly
Azure maintenance events move VMs; your IP changes
Multiple teams own different segments; no single change window
DB team, network team, app team all operate independently
Serialization, deserialization, header parsing all cost CPU
ADO protobuf vs. REST JSON performance difference
Your clients run on wildly different OS/runtime versions
VSTS web, VS IDE client, REST API, and CLI all talk to same svc

tables.heading_context: ## Theory Meets Practice: Key Papers → Production Systems
rows: Per-process logical clocks, detect causality violations
Consensus in asynchronous system with crash failures
Consensus impossible with 1 crash in fully async system
C + A + P not simultaneously achievable
Eventual consistency, vector clocks, sloppy quorum
Sorted string tables, LSM-tree, column families
Distributed commit log, consumer group model
